key_insight: The paper introduces MSVR, a variance-reduction estimator that can track many coupled inner functions using only one or a few stochastic block probes per iteration, enabling efficient finite-sum compositional optimization.
engineering_relevance: This matters for large-scale machine learning systems where compositional objectives and partial access to components make standard full-gradient tracking too expensive.
method: Multi-block-Single-probe Variance Reduction (MSVR) updates only O(1) sampled blocks of g(w) each step.
Builds optimization algorithms for FCCO across non-convex, convex, strongly convex, and PL settings.
Improves sample complexity, with stronger dependence on m when outer gradients are linear.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved sample-complexity results across multiple optimization regimes and empirical gains on multi-task deep AUC maximization.
watch_item: The approach relies on stochastic access to inner functions and careful block sampling, so practical performance may depend on oracle quality and sampling design.
paper_title: Solving Finite-sum Coupled Compositional Optimization via Multi-block-Single-probe Estimator
